english.title: Contravene requirement of constable to surrender liquor - Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement, imposed on you by a constable, to surrender **(..SPECIFY DESCRIPTION OF THE CONTAINER..), in your possession in a designated public place, namely **(..SPECIFY..), which was, or which the constable reasonably believed to be, alcohol, or a container for such liquor
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12(2)(b) and (4) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

english.notes:
From 20th October 2014, the power to make an order under section 13(2) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001 (power of local authority to designate public place for restrictions on alcohol consumption) is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to an order made before that date or anything done in connection with such an order. As such, this offence can still be committed in a public place designated by an order made before 20th October 2014.

(i) A constable who imposes a requirement on a person under section 12(2) shall inform the person concerned that failing without reasonable excuse to comply with the requirement is an offence
(ii) The Penalty Notice for Disorder was raised to £50 as from 1/11/04.
(iii) A constable who imposes a requirement on a person under Section 12(2) shall inform the person concerned that failing without reasonable excuse to comply with the requirement is an offence
(iv) The phrase "other than a sealed container" was removed by Schedule 7 to the LIcensing Act 2003.
